newsitem.title: UK: Med gasoline up, partly on higher U.S. prices.
newsitem.headline: Med gasoline up, partly on higher U.S. prices.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Monday, with traders saying gasoline edged up $1 a tonne in line with Rotterdam and firmer prices in the United States.
Premium unleaded nudged up to around $192 a tonne fob Italy but dealers said there was trade pressure to lift quotations above fixed price levels.
Naphtha was unchanged. End user demand remains thin and arbitrage to the U.S. does not work at current levels, traders said.
Gas oil was a mixed bag. Low sulphur material edged higher on a scarcity of material amid pockets of demand out of Italy, Spain and France.

An Italian refiner was offering some 50,000 tonnes worth of 0.05 percent at quotes fob hi +$5. Potential French buyers were heard bidding at around quotes fob hi +$2.5. Traders said they thought premiums around +$4-+$4.50 were more realistic.
In the 0.2 percent market premiums were discussed in the quotes fob hi flat/+50 cents area.
Traders said they were still waiting for the Russian July loading programme which they expected some time in the next week.
Traders said the picture was not clear for high sulphur fuel oil after a cargo held by a French refiner was reported sold for a hefty price out of Cartagena.
There was no immediate confirmation of the deal and the cargo was said on Friday to be offered at $85.50 cif.
Some traders said high sulphur fuel oil was flat to a bit pressured by plenty of avails.
"There's at least five or six cargoes being offered," one trader said, adding that the sellers were mostly negotiating with a major Italian refiner.
Traders said prices were a little vague but added that a June 18-20 loader of ISAB spec was on offer for $76 a tonne fob.
